To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the inactivation of DNA within irradiated pneumo-coccus cells is an exponential function of radiation dose, and (2) this radiosensitivity varies with the presence of oxygen and cysteamine in the same manner as the reproductive ability of the irradiated cells.

The radiosensitivity of DNA within irradiated pneumo-coccus cells has been determined by extracting the DNA after irradiation and measur-ing its ability to transform the cells to streptomycin resist-ance.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the DNA of the irradiated pneumococcal cell is inactivated in an exponential manner over several orders of magnitide, and that this is true for irradiation in the anoxic wet state, in the presence of oxygen, and in the presence of cysteamine.
